orgs.summary: UK government digital team. It created the GOV.UK site and maintains the GOV.UK Design System.

orgs.name: Gumroad
orgs.summary: A web site where creators sell products. Its 2021 redesign used thick black borders, hard shadows and flat bright colour, and spread neo-brutalism in product design.

orgs.name: Kinfolk
orgs.summary: A slow-living magazine with calm, natural-light photos. Its rooms mix Nordic and Japanese restraint.

orgs.name: LINE
orgs.summary: A messenger app that launched in 2011. Its sticker shop made drawn characters a main way to reply in a chat.

orgs.name: Microsoft Store
orgs.summary: The app store of Windows. With Windows 8 it sold "Metro-style apps" with flat tiles and large type.

orgs.name: Modernist Cuisine
orgs.summary: The six-volume book Modernist Cuisine: The Art and Science of Cooking, written by the team of Nathan Myhrvold at The Cooking Lab, with cut-section photographs.

orgs.name: Twitch
orgs.summary: A live video site, first for games. Its stream layouts, with a face window, chat and alert boxes, set the overlay look.

orgs.name: VSCO
orgs.summary: A photo app with presets that copy film stock. It spread grain and faded colour on phone photos.

orgs.name: Font Awesome
orgs.summary: An icon font and toolkit for the web. It ships solid, outline and duotone sets of the same icons.

orgs.name: Medium
orgs.summary: An online publishing platform. Designers wrote the articles there that named and explained new interface trends, glassmorphism among them.

orgs.name: Giphy
orgs.summary: A search site and library of looped clips. It turned the GIF into a reply that users pick by mood or tag.

orgs.name: itch.io
orgs.summary: An open store for independent games, where most PS1-style revival games are published.

orgs.name: Neocities
orgs.summary: A free host for hand-made personal web sites, started as a new GeoCities. Its users bring back pixel art, small buttons and cyber looks.

orgs.name: Ant Group
orgs.summary: Chinese financial services company and Alibaba affiliate. Its Ant User-Experience Design Team made Ant Design.

orgs.name: Brutalist Websites
orgs.summary: A web site that Pascal Deville started to collect raw, unstyled web sites. It made the name brutalist popular for this kind of web design.

orgs.name: Musical.ly
orgs.summary: A short-video app in which users mime songs in clips of 15 seconds. ByteDance bought it in 2017 and merged it into TikTok in 2018.

orgs.name: Discord
orgs.summary: A chat app for communities, with servers, text channels and voice channels.

orgs.name: GSA Technology Transformation Services
orgs.summary: Unit of the US General Services Administration. It maintains the U.S. Web Design System.

orgs.name: TikTok
orgs.summary: A video app of short vertical clips. Its feed set the form of vertical short-form video and spread the camcorder revival.

orgs.name: Haunted PS1
orgs.summary: A community of indie developers who make horror games in the style of the first PlayStation.

orgs.name: Lensa
orgs.summary: A photo editing app. Its Magic Avatars feature, from late 2022, returned packs of stylised portraits of one face.

orgs.name: BeReal
orgs.summary: A French photo app that asks users to post one back and one front camera photo within a short window. The post shows a time stamp and a late mark.

orgs.name: This Person Does Not Exist
orgs.summary: A web page that shows a new generated face on each reload. It made the generated headshot widely known.

orgs.name: CapCut
orgs.summary: A video-editing app by ByteDance with templates, speed curves and effects for short vertical clips.

orgs.name: Craiyon
orgs.summary: A free web page that turns a text prompt into a 3x3 grid of small, soft images. Users shared its grids as memes.

orgs.name: ChatGPT
orgs.summary: A chat assistant from OpenAI. Its single column of messages and its prompt box became the default look of an AI chat interface.

orgs.name: Midjourney
orgs.summary: A service that makes images from text prompts. Its users made and shared the glossy, hyperreal AI image.

emblem.credit: Original: Unknown author Vector: Aerra Carnicom

orgs.name: Abbey of Saint-Denis
orgs.summary: The abbey that Abbot Suger rebuilt from about 1135. Its choir of 1144 is widely seen as the first Gothic structure.

orgs.name: Andrew Grima, jeweller
orgs.summary: The London jewellery house of Andrew Grima. It made heavy, textured gold jewels with rough and uncut stones.

orgs.name: Arretine potteries
orgs.summary: The workshops of Arretium in Tuscany. They made stamped red-gloss tableware in moulds for the whole Roman world.

orgs.name: Arte della Lana
orgs.summary: The wool guild of Florence. It took over the patronage of the cathedral in 1331 and ran the dome competition in 1418.

orgs.name: Atlantic Terra Cotta Company
orgs.summary: A New York works that made glazed architectural terracotta for the towers, shops and cinemas of the 1920s and 1930s.

orgs.name: Basra potteries
orgs.summary: Potteries of the Abbasid port of Basra. Potters here made tin-glazed ware and, in the ninth century, painted it with the first lustre.

orgs.name: Battala printers of Calcutta
orgs.summary: The printers and cutters of the Battala quarter. From about 1816 they sold cheap books and woodcut sheets to a large bazaar public.

orgs.name: Bay Keramik
orgs.summary: A pottery of the Westerwald region of West Germany. It made many of the fat lava vases of the 1960s and 1970s.

orgs.name: Bou Inania Madrasa
orgs.summary: A Marinid madrasa in Fez, built in the 1350s for Sultan Abu Inan Faris. Zellige covers the lower walls of its court and its prayer hall.

orgs.name: Broderbund
orgs.summary: US software publisher. It released Myst for Mac OS in 1993. Myst became its best selling title.

orgs.name: Bunwon royal kiln
orgs.summary: The official kiln of the Joseon court in Gyeonggi province. It made the white porcelain for the palace, among it the large round moon jars.

orgs.name: Burslem potteries
orgs.summary: A group of small family potteries in the town of Burslem. They made slip-trailed dishes, jugs and posset pots from the 17th century.

orgs.name: Casa Pirota
orgs.summary: A maiolica workshop in Faenza that made sets of drug jars and painted dishes in the 16th century. It supplied pharmacies and hospitals.

orgs.name: Cersaie
orgs.summary: A yearly trade fair for ceramic tile and bath furnishing in Bologna, where the large format tile makers show new sizes and prints.

orgs.name: Charles Egan Gallery
orgs.summary: A New York gallery on East 57th Street. It held the 1948 show of de Kooning's black and white paintings.

orgs.name: Charles River Ventures
orgs.summary: US venture firm. It led the Series A round of 15 million dollars of Pebble in 2013.

orgs.name: Condé Nast
orgs.summary: US magazine publisher that Condé Montrose Nast built after he bought Vogue in 1909. It hired Edward Steichen in 1923.

orgs.name: Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute
orgs.summary: An online community that collects and names the looks of consumer goods and media from the 1970s on. It named Y2K and Frutiger Aero as aesthetics.

orgs.name: Della Robbia workshop
orgs.summary: The family workshop of Luca della Robbia in Florence. It made glazed terracotta reliefs for churches and chapels, and the family kept it in work to the 1520s.

orgs.name: Association of Devotees of St Joseph
orgs.summary: The group of Catholic donors that paid for the Sagrada Família. Its founder was the bookseller José María Bocabella.

orgs.name: Ding kilns
orgs.summary: The kiln sites of Quyang county. They made white porcelain bowls and dishes for the Song court and for trade.

orgs.name: Dong Ho village workshops
orgs.place: Dong Ho village, Bac Ninh, Vietnam
orgs.summary: The family workshops of Dong Ho village. They print the New Year woodblock paintings on paper with a shell-powder coat. The village had 17 print families in 1945.

orgs.name: DuPont
orgs.summary: US chemical company. It paid for pure research from 1927 and hired Wallace Carothers in 1928. His group made nylon.

orgs.name: Galerie Durand-Ruel
orgs.summary: The gallery of the dealer Paul Durand-Ruel. He met Monet and Pissarro in London in 1870 and began large purchases of Impressionist paintings in 1872.

orgs.name: Ford Foundation
orgs.summary: US foundation. It sponsored the Eameses' three-month study tour of India in 1958.

orgs.name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
orgs.summary: The studio of Frank Lloyd Wright in Oak Park. Here he and his assistants drew the Prairie houses and the first works of organic architecture.

orgs.name: Gangjin kilns
orgs.summary: The main kiln sites of Goryeo celadon, in the south-west of Korea. Potters here fired the green ware and inlaid it with white and black slip.

orgs.name: General Motors
orgs.summary: American car maker. In 1927 its president Alfred P. Sloan formed the Art and Colour Section with Harley Earl as director.

orgs.name: German government and War Ministry
orgs.summary: State bodies that gave starting capital to UFA in 1917 with Deutsche Bank. The Supreme Army Command wanted a state film corporation.

orgs.name: Gillows of Lancaster and London
orgs.summary: An English furniture maker that started in about 1730. Its mahogany furniture filled Georgian houses.

orgs.name: Gongxian kilns
orgs.summary: A group of Tang kilns in Henan that made sancai vessels and tomb figures. The kilns sent glazed horses and camels to the tombs of Luoyang and Chang'an.

orgs.name: Google
orgs.summary: US technology company. It bought YouTube in 2006 for 1.65 billion dollars in stock.

orgs.name: Government of Canada
orgs.summary: Federal government of Canada. It created the National Film Board by the National Film Act of 1939.

orgs.name: Grupo Cine Liberación
orgs.summary: An Argentine film group of Solanas, Getino and Vallejo. They made The Hour of the Furnaces and wrote Toward a Third Cinema, the best-known manifesto of Third Cinema.

statement.title: Toward a Third Cinema
statement.text: A film outside the studio and the art house is a tool of the struggle, and the screening is the start of a debate.

moves.text: The Hour of the Furnaces came out.
Solanas and Getino printed Toward a Third Cinema in the journal Tricontinental.

orgs.name: Guild of Saint Luke
orgs.summary: The city guild of painters in the Low Countries and elsewhere. A painter had to be a member to sell work and to train apprentices.

orgs.name: Gyeryongsan kilns
orgs.summary: Kilns at the foot of Mount Gyeryong in central Korea. They are well known for the bold brushed and stamped buncheong ware of the 15th and 16th centuries.

orgs.name: Haas Type Foundry
orgs.summary: A Swiss type foundry. It released Neue Haas Grotesk in 1957, which became Helvetica.

orgs.name: Hermès
orgs.summary: French luxury house. It bought 35 percent of the Jean Paul Gaultier label in 1999 and named Gaultier its creative director in 2003.

orgs.name: Høstutstillingen
orgs.summary: The annual autumn art exhibition of Norway. Norwegian painters started it to show their own work, and it carried national romantic painting.

orgs.name: Hyatt Foundation
orgs.summary: Sponsor of the Pritzker Architecture Prize. The Pritzker family funds the prize, which it founded in 1979.

orgs.name: Idea
orgs.summary: A Japanese magazine of graphic design. It printed the posters and marks of the Japanese modernists next to work from Europe and America.

orgs.name: Immaculate Heart College art department
orgs.summary: The art department of a college in Los Angeles where Corita Kent taught screen printing. The college closed in 1981.

orgs.name: Imprenta de Antonio Vanegas Arroyo
orgs.summary: A Mexico City press that sold cheap broadsides, songbooks and chapbooks. It used the metal-plate pictures of José Guadalupe Posada.

orgs.name: Ise katagami cutters
orgs.summary: The stencil cutters of Shiroko and Jike in Ise, now Suzuka. They cut the katagami stencils from layers of washi and supplied the dyers of Japan.

orgs.name: Iznik potteries
orgs.summary: The workshops of Iznik in north-west Anatolia. They made stonepaste dishes, tiles and lamps for the Ottoman court and for the mosques of Istanbul.

orgs.name: Jian kilns
orgs.summary: A group of dragon kilns in the hills of Fujian that made dark tea bowls for the Song market and the court. Thousands of kiln wasters lie on the sites today.

orgs.name: Jingdezhen imperial kilns
orgs.summary: The kilns at Jingdezhen that made porcelain for the court of the Ming and Qing emperors. Under Yongzheng and Qianlong they made the finest famille rose vases and bowls.

orgs.name: John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation
orgs.summary: US foundation that gives fellowships to artists and scholars. It gave Edward Weston the first photography fellowship in 1937.

orgs.name: Kerameikos potters' quarter
orgs.summary: The quarter of Athens where potters and vase painters worked beside the clay beds of the river. Black-figure and red-figure vases came from its workshops.

orgs.name: Kyoka poetry societies of Edo
orgs.summary: The comic-verse clubs of Edo. They paid artists and printers for surimono, small fine prints that carried a verse as a New Year card or a notice.

orgs.name: La Régalade
orgs.summary: A restaurant in the 14th arrondissement of Paris. Yves Camdeborde bought it in 1992 and cooked a fixed menu of bistro dishes there until he sold it.

orgs.name: Les Prés d'Eugénie
orgs.summary: A spa hotel and restaurant in the Landes. Michel Guérard cooked cuisine minceur here from 1974, and the restaurant held three Michelin stars from 1977.

orgs.name: Lira Nordestina
orgs.summary: A cordel press and woodcut workshop in Juazeiro do Norte. Sources differ on the year of its start.

orgs.name: Liulichang kilns
orgs.summary: The imperial kilns of Beijing that fired glazed tile for the palaces and temples of the Ming and Qing courts. The district Liulichang still carries their name.

orgs.name: Longquan kilns
orgs.summary: A large group of kilns in southern Zhejiang that made celadon from the Song dynasty. Their green ware went by sea to Japan, South-East Asia and the Near East.

orgs.name: L. Prang & Co.
orgs.summary: The colour lithography firm of Louis Prang. It printed trade cards, labels and Christmas cards with pictorial marks in the Victorian taste.

orgs.name: Manises potteries
orgs.summary: A town near Valencia where Moorish and then Christian potters made lustre ware. Its dishes went by ship to Italy, France and Burgundy.

orgs.name: Matsuki Heikichi (Daikokuya)
orgs.summary: A Tokyo publisher of woodblock prints. It issued the night views of Kobayashi Kiyochika.

orgs.name: Mino kilns
orgs.summary: The kilns of the Mino area in central Japan. In the Momoyama period they made Shino, Oribe and Setoguro tea ware in climbing kilns.

orgs.name: Mount Lebanon Shaker Society
orgs.summary: The main Shaker community. Its workshops made and sold plain chairs, boxes and furniture.

orgs.name: National Park Service
orgs.summary: US federal agency. In 1941 it signed a 180-day contract with Ansel Adams for mural-size park photographs.

orgs.name: Nordic Council of Ministers
orgs.summary: Body of the Nordic governments. Its food ministers backed New Nordic Cuisine from 2005.

orgs.name: Northwestern Terra Cotta Company
orgs.summary: A Chicago works that made architectural terracotta for the steel-frame buildings of the Chicago School. It supplied tile and ornament to many American cities.

orgs.name: Omuro kiln
orgs.summary: The kiln of Nonomura Ninsei below the temple of Ninna-ji in Kyoto. It made thin, enamelled tea ware for the court and the temples from the 1640s.

orgs.name: OpenAI
orgs.summary: US AI company. It released ChatGPT in November 2022. Microsoft is its main investor, with more than 13 billion dollars.

orgs.name: Opera di Santa Maria del Fiore
orgs.summary: The works office of Florence Cathedral. It ran the competition and the building site for the dome of Brunelleschi.

orgs.name: Pebble Technology
orgs.summary: Maker of the Pebble smartwatch. Its Kickstarter campaigns in 2012 and 2015 raised 10.3 and 20.3 million dollars.

orgs.name: Polycount
orgs.summary: An online forum and wiki for game artists, with much shared practice on hand-painted and PBR texture work.

orgs.name: Pont-Aven School
orgs.summary: A loose circle of painters in a Breton village, where an artists’ colony grew from the 1850s. Gauguin came in 1886; he and Bernard worked there on flat areas of colour with dark outlines, a manner that critics named Synthetism. The circle has no firm end date.

statement.text: Paint from memory and feeling, with flat colour and a strong outline, and do not copy the scene as the eye sees it.
statement.title: Synthetist method

moves.text: Sérusier painted The Talisman under the direction of Gauguin in the Bois d'Amour at Pont-Aven.
Gauguin, Bernard and their friends showed together as the Impressionist and Synthesist Group at the Café Volpini in Paris.

orgs.name: Prada Group
orgs.summary: Italian luxury group. It bought the houses of Helmut Lang and Jil Sander in 1999 and half of the Fendi stake that LVMH and Prada took in 1999.

orgs.name: Puppet Combo
orgs.summary: An American indie studio that makes low-poly horror games with a VHS and PS1 look.

orgs.name: Qin imperial tomb workshops
orgs.summary: State workshops near Mount Li that made the clay army for the tomb of the First Emperor. Each master stamped his name on the figures that he made.

orgs.name: Raeren potteries
orgs.summary: A cluster of stoneware workshops that made salt-glazed jugs, tankards and bottles with moulded reliefs from the 15th to the 17th century and sold them across Europe.

orgs.name: Senjafuda exchange clubs
orgs.summary: The clubs (nosatsu-kai) of collectors who swapped decorated name slips. The oldest invitation to an exchange meeting that is still known dates from 1799.

orgs.name: Thea Porter shop
orgs.summary: The Soho shop of Thea Porter. It sold caftans and long printed dresses of Middle Eastern cloth to the London scene of the late 1960s.

orgs.name: Thuringian state government
orgs.summary: State government that paid for the Bauhaus in Weimar. In 1924 a new conservative ministry cut the funding in half.

orgs.name: TIGSource
orgs.summary: An online forum for independent game makers where many early block and pixel games were shown.

orgs.name: UK government
orgs.summary: Government of the United Kingdom. It paid most of the cost of the 1951 Festival of Britain.

orgs.name: Urbino maiolica workshops
orgs.summary: A group of workshops in Urbino and the nearby towns of the Duchy. Their painters made the istoriato plates with large pictures for noble patrons.

orgs.name: US High Commission for Germany
orgs.summary: US occupation authority in Germany. Its High Commissioner John McCloy gave one million marks to the Ulm school project.

orgs.name: Warner-Amex Satellite Entertainment
orgs.summary: A joint venture of Warner Communications and American Express. It owned MTV at its start in 1981.

orgs.name: Warner Communications
orgs.summary: US media company. It bought Atari in 1976 for 28 million dollars and co-owned MTV through Warner-Amex.

orgs.name: Watanabe Woodblock Print Shop
orgs.summary: The print shop of Watanabe Shozaburo in Tokyo. It brought designer, carver and printer together to make the new landscape prints for export, in the shin-hanga movement.

orgs.name: Yangliuqing nianhua workshops
orgs.summary: The workshops of Yangliuqing town. They split the work of carving, printing and colour. Families in more than 30 villages added hand colour to the prints, and the sheets went to Beijing by canal.

orgs.name: Yixing kilns
orgs.summary: The dragon kilns and small workshops of the town of Yixing near Lake Tai. They made unglazed zisha teapots from the 16th century and still do.

orgs.name: Zhiying Studio
orgs.summary: A Shanghai studio round the calendar-poster painter Hang Zhiying. It drew the originals for the advertisers of yuefenpai posters.
